info.title: OpenDocRouter API
info.description: Parse PDFs and images to markdown with the model of your choice.

apiKey.description: An API key from the dashboard: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

status.description: `expired`: the request's hold ran out before it settled, so it's free. `rejected`: refused before it started (see `error_code`), and free.

error_code.description: Why a rejected or failed request ended, as an error code.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next pages.

results_expire_at.description: When the stored results are, or were, deleted. Null while processing or when nothing was stored (like setting `cache: false`).

markdown.description: Always in the POST response. From `GET /v1/parse/{id}`, with `expand=markdown` only.

cached.description: Served from the result cache, free.

PageLayout.description: For requests sent with `layout: true`: in the POST response, or from GET with `expand=layout`.

width.description: Points for a PDF page, pixels for an image.

elements.description: The markdown's elements in reading order, then pictures it doesn't mention.

lines.description: First and last line of the page markdown, 0-based and inclusive, splitting on "\n" only. Null for a picture the markdown doesn't mention.

boxes.description: In reading order. Empty when the element couldn't be placed; more than one when it's printed in pieces, such as a paragraph that continues in the next column.

r.description: Clockwise degrees about the box's centre, for text printed at an angle. x, y, w and h are then the unrotated box.

LayoutBox.description: Fractions of the page width and height, from the top left.

PageLayoutError.description: The page's markdown is still there; layout isn't charged.

code.description:
- `provider_error`: The provider returned an error.
- `rate_limited`: The provider rate-limited the page.
- `timeout`: The page didn't finish before the deadline.
- `output_truncated`: The output hit the token limit.
- `content_filtered`: The provider blocked the output, or the model declined.
- `repetitive_output`: The model got stuck repeating the same text.
- `invalid_output`: The model answered without transcribing the page.
- `empty_output`: The model returned no text.
- `at_capacity`: No provider capacity before the deadline.
- `unreadable_page`: The PDF opened, but this page couldn't be split or rendered.
- `response_too_large`: The page didn't fit in the response. Request it on its own with pages.
- `not_processed`: The async job ended before this page ran.

message.description: The page's own message in the POST response, or from GET with `expand=markdown`. Otherwise the code's standard description.

reason.description: The provider's own reason when it gave one, e.g. `RECITATION`, `SAFETY`, `refusal`, `max_tokens` or `repetition`.

code.description:
- `invalid_request`: The body, a parameter or the model is invalid.
- `url_not_allowed`: The document URL points somewhere we won't fetch.
- `unauthorized`: The API key is missing, unknown or revoked.
- `insufficient_credits`: Not enough available credit to hold the request's maximum cost.
- `account_paused`: The account is paused.
- `not_found`: No such request, job, upload or path.
- `gone`: The request's stored results were deleted, by the caller or 24 hours after it finished.
- `results_not_stored`: The request's results weren't stored: it was a sync request without `cache: true`, so they were returned once, in the POST response.
- `too_large`: The body, document or page selection is over a limit.
- `unsupported_type`: Only PDF, PNG and JPEG are supported.
- `unreadable_document`: The document couldn't be fetched or opened.
- `rate_limited`: Too many requests or jobs at once, too many GETs in a minute, or the provider is rate-limiting.
- `at_capacity`: The model is at capacity or temporarily unavailable.
- `model_starting`: A hosted model is starting up. Retry in a few minutes.
- `internal_error`: Something went wrong on our side.

required_usd.description: `insufficient_credits` only: what the request needs available.

available_usd.description: `insufficient_credits` only: what the account has available.

document.description: A URL, inline base64 data, or an upload.

mode.description: `sync` parses the document in this request and returns 200 with results for every page, up to the model's `max_sync_pages`. `async` returns 202 parses it as a job pollable on `GET /v1/parse/<id>`, up to 500 pages. It needs `cache: true`. Defaults to `sync`.

pages.description: 1-based pages and ranges. Defaults to every page. At most the model's `max_sync_pages` in sync mode, 500 in async mode.

cache.description: Store the results, encrypted, for 24 hours: `GET /v1/parse/{id}?expand=markdown` reads them and `DELETE /v1/parse/{id}` deletes them sooner. Pages your account already has stored for the same document, model and `layout` are served from them, free. Required for `async`. Defaults to false.

layout.description: Add each ok page's `layout`: its elements, the markdown lines each one spans and where it's printed. Adds $0.20 per million tokens to pages whose layout comes back. Defaults to false.

url.description: A public URL to fetch, up to 50 MB.

balance_usd.description: Everything paid in, minus everything charged.

available_usd.description: What a new request can use: balance minus reserved.

version.description: Changes whenever output behavior can change.

max_sync_pages.description: Most pages a `mode: "sync"` request can take.

score.description: Mean of the five category scores.

visual_grounding.description: How well `layout: true` places each element on the page.

parsebench.description: ParseBench scores for this version. Null while benchmarking.

max_charge_per_page_usd.description: The most one page can be charged, which is what a request holds per page.

avg_charge_per_page_usd.description: What a typical page costs at these prices: the mean tokens per page this version used on ParseBench. An estimate; your pages may differ. Null until benchmarked.

page_latency.description: How long one page takes on this version, from every successful page it has parsed. Pages in a request run in parallel. Null until enough pages are measured.

cold_starts.description: True for models on GPUs we start on demand. After the model sits idle, a request waits up to 45 seconds for one to start, or fails with `model_starting` if it takes longer, without being charged.

post.description:
`mode: "sync"` (the default) parses the document in this request and returns 200 with every page, up to the model's `max_sync_pages`. `mode: "async"`, which needs `cache: true`, returns 202 and parses up to 500 pages as a job; `GET /v1/parse/{id}?expand=markdown` has the results. At most 5 async requests run at once per account, and at most 300 requests a minute.

Admission holds the most the request could cost; it's released, less the actual charge, when the request finishes. Failed pages are free.

200.description: `mode: "sync"` only: parsed. Some pages may have failed (`partial`).

202.description: `mode: "async"` only: accepted as a job. Poll `GET /v1/parse/{id}`.

get.description:
Works for any request. While it runs, `pages` is empty and `pages_done` counts progress. Then it returns every page, unless the expanded results are over 4 MB: then `has_more` is true, and you ask again with `cursor` set to `next_cursor`.

Markdown and layout are opt-in, with `expand`, and only requests sent with `cache: true` store them, for 24 hours after they finish. Without `expand`, this never returns document text.

schema.description: `markdown` adds each ok page's markdown, `layout` its layout (for requests sent with `layout: true`), and `markdown,layout` both. For requests sent with `cache: true`.

parameters.description: `markdown` adds each ok page's markdown, `layout` its layout (for requests sent with `layout: true`), and `markdown,layout` both. For requests sent with `cache: true`.
parameters.name: expand

delete.description: Deletes the results stored with `cache: true`, so they're also no longer served from the cache. A running job stops before its next chunk. Pages already parsed are still charged. The request's status and cost stay available.

post.summary: Get a one-time URL to upload large documents
post.description: For documents over 4 MB. PUT the file to `upload_url` (up to 50 MB), then send `document: {upload_id}` to `POST /v1/parse`. An upload can be used once, and expires 60 minutes after it's created. An account can have 100 unused uploads at once.
